mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC rose in each of the last two weekly readings (-16.4, then -15.0, then -12.6) and every co-moving activity series except WORKPLACES is also improving, so this momentum carries into the next four weeks and the forward 28-day mean exceeds the trailing 28-day mean of -14.6.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC moved -16.4 to -15.0 to -12.6 over the last three weekly means
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is at or below -14.6, meaning the two-consecutive-week rising sequence reverses instead of continuing.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS jumped 17.2 points week-on-week from -27.1 to -9.9, marking the spring outdoor-activity transition; the extra out-of-home social trips convert into retail-and-recreation spending, lifting RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 15 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -38.7 at t-2w to -27.1 at t-1w to -9.9 at t-0w
regime_hint: spring seasonal transition into warmer weeks
failure_condition: Following a PARKS week-on-week rise greater than 15 points, the next 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not above its trailing 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT improved for three straight weeks (-42.9 to -40.4 to -38.3) while RESIDENTIAL stays pinned near +6.7, so trips are being reallocated from home to non-work destinations; the joint pattern raises RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves at least 2 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL stays above +5
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL held between +5.6 and +6.7 in all four weekly means
regime_hint: steady state with elevated remote work
failure_condition: In weeks where TRANSIT gains at least 2 points and RESIDENTIAL exceeds +5, the forward 14-day RETAIL_REC mean is not above the trailing 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The 13.5-point single-week WORKPLACES drop to -28.6 is a holiday artefact because TRANSIT and RETAIL_REC did not fall with it; the holiday suppresses retail only transiently, so RETAIL_REC rebounds the following week and the four-week mean rises.

evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -15.1 to -28.6 at t-0w while TRANSIT rose from -40.4 to -38.3
regime_hint: holiday week embedded in a recovery
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week after a greater-than-10-point single-week WORKPLACES drop unconfirmed by TRANSIT, and the 28-day forward mean stays below the trailing mean.

mechanism_narrative: A WORKPLACES reading below -20 sustained for two consecutive weeks indicates a real employment-activity contraction rather than a holiday, removing commuter-linked disposable footfall from retail corridors and pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.

failure_condition: When WORKPLACES holds below -20 for two consecutive weeks, the subsequent 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is at or above the trailing 28-day mean.

evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed between -2.3 and -3.7 across all four weekly means
failure_condition: The next-week RETAIL_REC reading falls below the prior week whenever GROCERY_PHARM is below -2.0 and RETAIL_REC rose at least 1 point week-on-week.

regime_hint: phased reopening with capacity limits being lifted
